column2: Having remembered and given rochana, one should do the cleansing and the rest; with the gift of jaggery, salt and coriander one should dismiss them,
together with the bearers of the teacher's form, with the heart-mantra or with Om; with clay, cow-dung, cow-urine and ash, with water in between,
one should bathe with the five cow-products preceded by the five nectars; the drying with astringents or with water of all herbs;
with white flowers, fruits, gold, jewels, horn and barley-water; likewise with a thousand streams and with water of divine herbs,
with water from sacred places, Ganga water, sandal-water, with pots of milk-ocean water and the like and with water from Shiva's pot.
The drying and anointing with fragrances, sandal and the rest; having worshipped with Brahmas, flowers, armor and red garments,
having waved lights in red form preceded by protective marks; with ghee, herbs, water, milk, kusha and the rest indicated for arghya,
with materials, praises and the rest one should worship the satisfied one with the Purusha-atom. Having rinsed, with the heart-mantra one should say to the god: "Rise, Lord."
By the Brahma-chariot alone one should swiftly carry the god and the materials; in the pavilion at the west door one should place him on the couch.
From Shakti to the end of the powers one should place on an auspicious seat; at the west end of the pedestal one should place the Brahma stone then.
Having prepared the weapon, missile, the sleep-pot gained by a hundred, and the fixed seat, and in the Shiva corner, having given arghya with the heart-mantra,
having raised the linga with the head toward the east on the said seat, one should place on it in the order of creation the salutation of Dharma and the rest.
One should give incense after worshipping, and likewise garments with the armor-mantra; food for the household's benefit one should give with the heart-mantra according to ability;
a vessel with ghee and honey for anointing at the foot; and the teacher standing there, the collection of the thirty-six principles
from Shakti up to earth with their own presiding lords, having placed with flower garlands, one should arrange the three sections;
the round of the eighth part from the fourth, up to the Maya-region power; there the Self-principle called knowledge, Shiva, in the order of creation;
in each portion having placed Brahma, Vishnu and Hara as lords, forms and lords of forms in order from the east:
earth, fire, sacrificer, sun, water, wind, moon, space — one should place their forms and their lords.
Sarva, Pashupati, Ugra, Rudra, Bhava, Makheshvara, Mahadeva and Bhima — these are the mantras denoting them.
La Va Sha Sha Cha Ya Sa and the letter Ha of three measures; Om, the heart-syllable, or the root-mantra, or in some places;
in a sacrifice with five pits one should place five forms: earth, water, fire, wind and space.
In order their five lords: Brahma, Dharanidhara, Rudra, Ishvara, and Sadashiva, by the method of creation, the mantra-knower.
For the seeker of liberation: Nivritti and the rest, Ajata and the rest, their lords; or one should place everywhere the three principles, the pervading cause.
In the pure Self the lords of knowledge; in the impure the leaders of the worlds; the lords of forms and the enjoying ones, the mantra-leaders are to be seen.
Twenty-five, likewise eight, five and three in order; the principles of these and of their lords, of Indra and the others, then as follows:

Om Ham, homage to the Shakti-principle, and so on; "Om Ham, homage to the lord of the Shakti-principle"; "Om Ham, homage to the Earth form; Om Ham, homage to Shiva, lord of the Earth form"; "Om Ham, homage to the Water form; Om Ham, homage to Brahma, lord of the form"; "Om Ham, homage to Rudra, lord of the Shiva-principle" — uttering from the navel-bulb, the spreading sound of a bell, from abandoning the cause beginning with Brahma resting at the twelve-end,
the mantra and the mind divided, like the savor of attained bliss; having brought from the twelve-end the partless, pervading Shiva,
endowed with thirty-eight digits, shining with a thousand rays, made of all power, with limbs, having meditated one should place in the linga.
This is the placing of life in the linga, accomplishing all aims. The placing in the pedestal and the rest is now told:
the pedestal, bathed, anointed with sandal and the rest, covered with good cloths, and in the cavity with the mark of the yoni,
joined with five jewels and the rest, standing north of the linga, with placements made like the linga, one should worship by rule.
At the root of the linga one should place the stone, bathed and prepared, ending in Shakti, and the bull likewise,
with Om first, "Hum Pum Hrim" or any one of the middle; the pedestal joined with the power of action, the stone in the form of support,
one should make three enclosures with ash, darbha and sesame; for protection one should worship the guardians of the world with weapons outside.

Om Hum Hram, homage to the power of action; Om Hum Hram Hah, Mahagauri, beloved of Rudra, svaha — on the pedestal; "Om Ham, homage to the support-power; Om Ham, homage to the bull" — the holder, the shining, fierce, Jyotsna, these strong ones; likewise Dhatri and Vidhatri, or one may place five leaders.
Vama, Jyeshtha, Kriya, Jnana, Bodha — or one may place three. Kriya, Jnana and Iccha as before in the forms of peace.
Tamas, Moha, Kshama, Nishtha, Mrityu, Maya, Bhava, Jvara — and five great delusions and Ghora, the three fevers;
or three, Kriya and Jnana, and likewise Badha the lead; in the three principles beginning with the Self, one should place in the intense forms.
Here too, in the pedestal, the Brahma stone and so on by rule, with Gauri and the other coverings, one should do all as before.
Having thus done the placing and gone to the pit, then in the pit's middle Maheshana, on the girdles Maheshvara,
the power of action and others, and nada on the lip one should place; the pot, the platform-fire and lords, the joining of channels then,
the power equal to a lotus-fiber rising by the upward breath, entering by the sun's path, going out, risen,
and again entering by the void path — one should contemplate one's own. Thus everywhere it should be joined, and mutually by the lords of forms.
Having worshipped the supporting power and satisfied it in the pit in order, the principles, lords of principles, forms and lords of forms with ghee and the rest,
having worshipped and satisfied them in their presence with Samhita atoms, one should offer a hundred, a thousand or half with the full oblation.
The lords of forms, principles and lords, and the Kareṇukas, likewise having satisfied in presence, the form-lords too should offer.
Then with Brahmas and limbs according to material and time, having satisfied the power, sprinkled with pot-water from the kusha root,
having touched the root of the linga they should repeat by the number of the oblations; they should make presence with the heart and covering with armor.
Thus having purified Brahma and the rest up to Vishnu for purification, having done everything as before, the number of oblations, repetition and the rest,
by joining of the middle and tip of kusha one should touch the middle and tip of the linga. How the joining is done is now told here:

Om Ham Ham Om Om Om Em Om Bhum Bhum, homage to the outer form; Om Ham Vam Am Om Am Sham Om Bhum Bhum Vam, homage to the fire-form — and thus one should join with the forms of the sacrificer and the rest. Even in the five-form one, the joining is thus with the heart-mantra and the rest,
with the root or with one's own seeds; in the three-principle one it is to be known. In the stone-pedestal bulls thus, full, unbroken, with the coverings.
For purification of share and non-share one should do a hundred and more oblations; for removing faults of deficiency and the rest a hundred and eight with Shiva-mantra.
Having offered, one should report to Shiva's ear the work done: "This work, complete with this, in your power, by me, Lord:
Om, homage to the Lord Rudra; Rudra, homage to you; whether complete or incomplete by rule, let it be completed by your own power and accepted."
Om Hrim, O Shankari, complete, svaha — on the pedestal. Then the knower should place on the linga the "Kriya" in the form of the seat:
one should place the power in the form of support above the Brahma stone. Having bound for seven nights or five nights or three nights,
or one night, or immediate dwelling. Without dwelling the sacrifice done also gives fruit.
With one's own mantras daily a hundred and a hundred oblations are to be given; and one should offer worship of Shiva's pot and the rest, and the offering of the directions;
dwelling with the teacher and others at night, preceded by restraint. That is called the state of "dwelling," from the root "vas."
Joined with all seeds and gold one should place it; made of gold, silver or of all metals;
gold with rice-gruel, then one should place the lotus-stalk; a seat of the god of gods from Shakti to the form;
having prepared, then smeared with pudding or guggulu, having covered the pit with cloth, protected by armor and the weapon,
having given the offering to the guardians of the quarters, and rinsed, the teacher, with Shiva, or for removing the fault of joining of the stone and the pit,
or with the weapon one should rightly offer a hundred with the full oblation; having satisfied the site-deities with one oblation each,
having raised the god with the heart-mantra, the seat with auspicious things and the rest, the teacher should go in front of the god with the form-lords standing in the directions;
with four it should be done behind the god's sacrifice. Having circumambulated the temple and the rest, facing the door called Bhadra,
having established the linga and given arghya, one should install it in the temple. By the door, by the door-bond, by the door-region, the stone;
in a door-bond without crest, with half of that or without it; avoiding touching the door, Maheshvara only by the door;
at the beginning of a temple even by the corner one should enter. This same rule is to be known for a manifest linga everywhere.
Entry into a house by the door is also stated by people; by entering through a wrong door they know the house leads to loss of lineage.
Then having established the linga on the pedestal facing the door, with the sound of trumpets and auspicious songs, with durva and rice,
having said "Rise" with the heart, one should recite the Mahapashupata. Having removed the pot from the pit, the teacher with the form-lords,
having upheld the mantra, anointed with saffron and the rest, having meditated on the unity of Shakti and the possessor of Shakti, and protected,
having uttered the root-mantra ending in dissolution one should touch and set it in the pit — by a part of the Brahma portion, or by two parts,
or half, or by an eighth part of all, the entry; having made the lead navel-long and well composed,
having filled the pit with sand one should say "Be steady." Then, the linga being steady, having meditated on the form with parts,
uttering the root-mantra ending in Shakti, one should place the partless by creation. When the linga being installed leans toward the south,
with the mantra of that quarter's lord ending with the full oblation, with a fee, in the left place, or crooked, or shaken, or cracked,
one should offer a hundred with the root-mantra or the many-formed; in other faults too one should take refuge in the peace-rite of Shiva.
